assign.request: Fix the worst mobile-only regression found by the 2026-08-17 mobile sweep: /framework/ai/ scores 82/B at 1280 and 58/F at 390 -- a task card's title-and-tag row overflows 119px (36% of its own width) past the card's right edge on 15 of ~105 cards. Dispatched by mastermind-layout.
steps: Decide phone behavior for title+tag row
Implement fix at correct CSS rung
Re-run analyze() to confirm no new finding

log.msg: Reproduced. analyze() at 390: score 48/F (baseline 1280 is 84/B, matches the reported 82/B). Leading finding: rule=escape, sev=high, sel=div.ai-card.surface, worst child div.ai-who.flex.gap 119px outside the card (36% of its width), n=15; paired doc-overflow finding (n=9, extends past viewport) and a cramped finding, also high. Proposed fix from the tool: min-width:0 on .ai-card.surface. Confirmed by eye: shot at 390 matches the mobile-sweep screenshot (ai-index-card-escape-390.png) -- element-pages card title+tag row and body text both cut off at the card edge.

assign.now: reading ext/AITask readme traps + card.js + ai.css

log.msg: Read ai.css and readme.md. .ai-card is a grid (who|what|figures) with an existing @container (width < 44em) rule that already collapses to a single column and stacks .ai-figures -- this IS the mobile pattern this module uses (a container query keyed to the cards own container-type: inline-size on .ai-list, not a viewport breakpoint, matching card.js/readme.md Card layout is a container query, not a viewport one). The bug is inside that existing rule, not a missing one: grid-template-columns: 1fr keeps 1frs content-based automatic minimum, so .ai-who (dot + title + status/tag row) refuses to shrink below its own min-content and spills past the card instead of collapsing to it. Read last nights ai-rail-mobile trap first per the brief -- different mechanism (flex-basis/max-height on a routed rail), same lesson (reuse the existing responsive hook, do not invent a second one): the fix here reuses the SAME @container rule, just gives its one column a floor.

assign.now: deciding phone behavior for the title+tag row

log.msg: Decision: wrap, not stack or truncate. The tag (.ai-tag) already wraps under the title via its own flex.gap.wrap row (card.js line 68) -- that part of the design was already right. The task NAME must stay whole (its the primary identifier on a working log a developer scans by name) so truncation is wrong; the row itself just needs to be ALLOWED to shrink to the cards width so wrapping can happen at all, which is a track-sizing bug, not a content decision. layout-design bounds.md: every track needs a floor AND a ceiling, minmax(0, ...) and min-width:0 are the same declaration in two syntaxes.

Fix applied: ext/AITask/ai.css, @container (width < 44em) block -- .ai-card grid-template-columns changed from 1fr to minmax(0, 1fr). One declaration, reuses the existing container-query mechanism, no new breakpoint, inside the fence (ai.css). Verified candidate via Playwright CSS injection before editing the file, then re-verified against the real edited file with identical results.

Verified with headless Playwright (probe scripts in scratchpad) against the live dev server (port 80, not restarted). analyze() score/grade: 390 48/F -> 84/B (high 3->0); 720 82/B unchanged; 1280 84/B unchanged; 3440 61/D unchanged (its 2 high measure findings are pre-existing, outside this @container(<44em) rules reach, confirmed identical baseline with/without the fix). DOM measurement across ALL 107 .ai-card rows at 390: max .ai-who overflow past its card was 118px before, 0px after -- every overflowing card fixed, not just the sampled one. The single worst card from the mobile-sweep finding (title element-pages, 118px measured here vs 119px reported) individually confirmed fixed: before/after crops saved to scratchpad (before-card-element-pages.png, after-card-element-pages.png). Longest single title on the dashboard (improve-daily-task-dashboard, 28 chars) never overflowed even pre-fix -- the trigger is the muted status/tab-title text width, not title length alone; the fix is structural (track floor) so it covers every card regardless of which part of the row is long.

assign.outcome: **Reproduced and fixed.** /framework/ai/ at 390: analyze() 48/F (matching the reported 58/F) -> 84/B, all three high-severity findings (escape, doc-overflow, cramped) gone. Cause: ext/AITask/ai.css's existing @container (width < 44em) rule already collapses .ai-card to one column, but `grid-template-columns: 1fr` kept 1fr's content-based auto-minimum, so .ai-who (dot+title+status/tag row) refused to shrink and spilled up to 119px past the card on 15/107 cards. Fix: one declaration, `1fr` -> `minmax(0, 1fr)`, same rule, no new breakpoint (ext/AITask/ai.css). Decision: the row WRAPS (title stays whole, tag drops below it) -- truncating the task name was rejected since it's the primary scan key on a working log; the tag already wrapped correctly, the row just needed to be allowed to shrink. Verified: 390 84/B, 720/1280/3440 byte-identical to baseline (rule only fires <44em); DOM-measured across all 107 cards, max overflow 118px->0px; the reported worst card (element-pages, 118px) individually confirmed fixed, before/after crops in scratchpad; rule-type set after is a strict subset of before (no new finding traded in). Documented in ext/AITask/readme.md Traps, beside last night's ai-rail-mobile entry.
